w10_P4_002458: The figure the depot manager finally wants is twice the total kinetic energy of a whole rake of 12 identical ore carts, expressed in kilojoules, because the rake makes 2 loaded runs per shift. Each cart has a mass of 50000 g. On the downhill section every cart rolls at a speed, in metres per second, equal to 3 times the sum of 3 and 8. Work out the kinetic energy of a single cart in joules, then the total for all 12 carts, convert that total to kilojoules, and finally double it for the 2 runs. What is the resulting value in kJ?
w10_P4_002459: A test engineer needs the combined push that a rig must supply to 11 identical sleds at once, in newtons. Each sled has a mass of 87000 g. The rig's controller sets the acceleration of a sled, in metres per second squared, from a calibration rule: take the instantaneous rate of change of the curve 3x^3 - 2x^2 with respect to x at the point x = 1, subtract 6 from it, then add 20. With the acceleration fixed, determine the push needed for one sled, and then the total for all 11 sleds moving together. What is that combined push in N?
w10_P4_002462: The quantity a wind-tunnel technician records at the end of the day is the total energy, in kilojoules, delivered over 4 identical launches of a test carriage. For a single launch, the carriage of mass 22 kg reaches a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 3x^3 + 4x^2 with respect to x evaluated at x = 2. From the carriage's kinetic energy in joules at that speed, 4 J is deducted for the energy absorbed by the release latch. The corrected per-launch energy is converted to kilojoules, and then multiplied by 4 for the 4 launches. What is the recorded total in kJ?
w10_P4_002467: A robotics club fires a 16000 g projectile from a pneumatic launcher along a 40 m test corridor. The launch speed, in metres per second, is set equal to the number of different ways of choosing 2 members from a team of 7. Compute the projectile's kinetic energy in joules at that speed and express it in kilojoules. The launcher's accumulator then adds 17 kJ of stored energy to that figure, after which 15 kJ is subtracted to account for the energy bled off through the exhaust valve. What is the remaining energy in kJ?
w10_P4_002472: A shipping company tests 12 identical parcel sleds on a chute in a warehouse kept at 25 degrees Celsius. Each sled has a mass of 53000 g. Its speed in metres per second is found by taking the larger of the two values of x that make x^2 - 6x + 8 equal to zero, reducing that value by 1, and then increasing the result by 7. Find the kinetic energy in joules of one sled at that speed, then the total for all 12 sleds, and express that total in kilojoules. What is the total kinetic energy of the 12 sleds in kJ?
w10_P4_002473: In a foundry, a trolley of mass 55 kg is pulled along a 30 m rail by a winch cable. The trolley's acceleration in metres per second squared is the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. Find the pull needed to give the trolley that acceleration, in newtons, and convert it to kilonewtons. The cable also carries a steady 9 kN preload and a further 7 kN from a counterweight, both of which add to that figure, while a 5 kN reduction is applied for the winch's brake assist. What is the resulting cable tension in kN?
w10_P4_002475: The number the crane inspector ultimately writes down is the load rating for the full set of 11 hoist lines, in kilonewtons. Each hoist line carries 10 identical lifting frames, and each frame has a mass of 42000 g and a hook width of 3 m. During the test lift, every frame accelerates upward at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 8 equals zero. Find the net push required on a single frame in newtons, convert it to kilonewtons, multiply by the 10 frames on one line, and add the line's own 9 kN safety allowance. The inspector's rating is that per-line figure multiplied by the 11 lines. What is the rating in kN?
w10_P4_002476: A rocket-sled facility runs a test sled of mass 194000 g. The sled's acceleration in metres per second squared is obtained by taking the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0, multiplying it by 6, and adding 18. Determine the thrust needed to give the sled that acceleration, in newtons. The facility couples a second identical sled behind the first, so the thrust supplied is 2 times that amount, and the same double-sled run is performed simultaneously on 6 parallel tracks. What is the total thrust supplied across all 6 tracks, in N?
w10_P4_002484: A cargo elevator platform in a warehouse has a mass of 158000 g. Its upward acceleration in metres per second squared is set by adding 10 to the rate of change of the curve 4x^3 + 4x^2 with respect to x at x = 1. Find the push in newtons that produces this acceleration. A counterweight supplies 21 N of that push, so the hoist motor must provide the remainder. Express the motor's share in kilonewtons. What is the motor's share in kN?
w10_P4_002490: A go-kart with its driver has a combined mass of 89000 g. On the launch straight the kart's acceleration in metres per second squared is 14 more than the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0. Work out the driving force in newtons needed to give the kart that acceleration. The engine must supply an additional 10 N to overcome the rolling resistance of the tyres, so add 10 N to the driving force. Express the total engine force in kilonewtons. What is the total engine force in kN?
w10_P4_002493: The final figure a stage-rigging crew needs is the total force, in newtons, for 3 identical truss sections, each of which is driven by 7 identical motors. Each motor moves a load of mass 37000 g. The load's acceleration in metres per second squared is found by taking the rate of change of the curve 2x^3 + 6x^2 with respect to x at x = 1 and subtracting 14. Determine the force one motor must exert on its load in newtons, then the combined force of the 7 motors on one truss section, and then the total for all 3 sections. What is that total force in N?
w10_P4_002499: The value the packaging engineer reports is the total kinetic energy, in kilojoules, of 3 batches of parcels, where each batch contains 4 identical parcels. Each parcel has a mass of 7 kg. On the conveyor every parcel moves at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. Find the kinetic energy in joules of one parcel, multiply by 4 for a batch, multiply by 3 for all the batches, and convert the result to kilojoules. What is the total in kJ?
w10_P4_002501: A maglev test bogie of mass 116000 g runs in a hall kept at 18 degrees Celsius. Its acceleration in metres per second squared equals the area under the curve 3x^2 + 2x between x = 0 and x = 2. Find the propulsive force in newtons needed to give the bogie that acceleration. The bogie is one of 6 identical bogies coupled into a train, so multiply the force by 6 to get the force for the whole train, and convert that to kilonewtons. The guideway adds 9 kN of magnetic braking drag that the propulsion must also overcome, so add 9 kN. What is the total propulsive force in kN?
w10_P4_002514: What the range officer wants at the end of the session is a single energy figure in kilojoules: the total for 4 rounds of firing, each round consisting of 3 identical shots, plus an 11 kJ allowance for the energy stored in the launcher's spring. Each shot propels a 53 kg dummy payload along a 120 m range. The payload's speed in metres per second is the second derivative of 1x^3 + 2x^2 with respect to x evaluated at x = 2. Find the kinetic energy of one payload in joules and convert it to kilojoules; multiply by 3 for one round, then by 4 for all rounds, and finally add the 11 kJ allowance. What is the officer's figure in kJ?
w10_P4_002516: The number the harbour master signs off is the combined mooring rating for 11 identical berths, in kilonewtons. At each berth, 10 identical fenders share the load, and each fender must be rated for the force found as follows. A buoy of mass 35000 g, floating 4 m from the quay, is accelerated by the surge at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the greatest common divisor of 269 and 168. Find the force in newtons that gives the buoy that acceleration, add 17 N for the drag of its tether, and convert the result to kilonewtons. Multiply that per-fender figure by the 10 fenders to get one berth's rating, and then by the 11 berths. What is the combined rating in kN?
w10_P4_002521: The quantity the lab needs is the kinetic energy, in joules, of a 44 kg test dummy at the moment its sled is released. The sled's speed in metres per second is dialled in by the control software as follows: start with the greatest common divisor of 338 and 215, multiply it by 8, multiply the result by 9, subtract 30, and then add 10. The dummy sits on a sled running along a rail in a crash-test hall. Using the mass and the computed speed, determine the dummy's kinetic energy. What is that energy in J?
w10_P4_002523: A delivery drone of mass 24000 g cruises at a speed in metres per second equal to 2 times the sum of 8 and 11. Find the drone's kinetic energy in joules at that speed. Its battery management system adds 20 J for the energy stored in the spinning rotors, and the total is converted to kilojoules. From that figure 2 kJ is subtracted for the reserve that must remain untouched. The operator flies 11 identical drones, so the per-drone result is multiplied by 11. What is the fleet total in kJ?
w10_P4_002530: What the site foreman ultimately needs is the combined rating of 9 identical hydraulic rams, in kilonewtons. Each ram handles 8 identical pallets, and each pallet of mass 98 kg must be accelerated at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the number of ways of choosing 4 items from a set of 6. Find the force in newtons required for one pallet and convert it to kilonewtons. Multiply by the 8 pallets to get one ram's demand, then subtract 8 kN for the assistance provided by the ram's return spring. The foreman's figure is that per-ram result multiplied by the 9 rams. What is it in kN?
w10_P4_002533: The result the flight-test engineer wants is the energy, in kilojoules, for 3 identical catapult launches after all corrections have been applied. A single launch propels a 52000 g drone to a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 3x^3 - 2x^2 with respect to x at x = 3. Find the drone's kinetic energy in joules, subtract 2 J for the energy lost in the release hook, and convert the result to kilojoules. Then subtract a further 29 kJ that the catapult's flywheel retains after each launch. The engineer multiplies this corrected per-launch figure by 3 for the 3 launches. What is the total in kJ?
w10_P4_002543: The figure the safety auditor records is the total energy, in kilojoules, absorbed by a crash barrier over 8 test sessions of 4 impacts each, plus a 17 kJ allowance for the barrier's own spring-back. In each impact a 36 kg trolley, launched from a ramp 5 m long, strikes the barrier at a speed in metres per second equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0. Find the trolley's kinetic energy in joules and convert it to kilojoules; multiply by 4 for one session and then by 8 for all sessions, and finally add the 17 kJ allowance. What is the recorded total in kJ?
w10_P4_002547: A regenerative-braking rig on a workshop bench captures the motion of a 55 kg flywheel cart, which runs on a track 12 m long. The cart moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0. Find the cart's kinetic energy in joules and express it in kilojoules; this is the energy recovered into the battery in one cycle. During the same cycle a charger adds 24 kJ to the battery and the motor draws 27 kJ from it. The rig runs 11 identical cycles. What is the net change in the battery's stored energy over the 11 cycles, in kJ (negative if a loss)?
w10_P4_002551: A mine hoist raises 10 identical skips, each carrying 12 identical ore bins, up a shaft 250 m deep. Each ore bin has a mass of 81 kg and accelerates upward at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. Find the net force in newtons on one bin, then the force for the 12 bins in a skip, then the force for all 10 skips. The hoist cable must also carry an extra 14 N for its own attachment hardware, so add 14 N. Express the result in kilonewtons. What is the cable force in kN?
w10_P4_002552: A luggage-handling system on an airport concourse 60 m wide moves 18 kg suitcases along a belt. The belt speed in metres per second is 8 times the greatest common divisor of 298 and 115. Find the kinetic energy in joules of one suitcase at that speed. There are 5 suitcases on the belt at any moment, so multiply by 5, and then add 17 J for the energy stored in the belt's tensioning spring. The system has 5 identical belts, so multiply the result by 5. What is the total energy in J?
w10_P4_002555: The engineer is after the adjusted holding figure, in kilonewtons, for a clamp on a test block, and the clamp's rating is obtained only after two corrections. The block has a mass of 12000 g and accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0. Find the force in newtons that gives the block that acceleration and convert it to kilonewtons. To that figure a 16 kN preload is added, and then a 17 kN hydraulic relief is subtracted. What is the adjusted figure in kN (negative if the relief exceeds the load)?
w10_P4_002568: A bowling-alley pinsetter returns a 15000 g ball along a track at a speed in metres per second equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0. Find the ball's kinetic energy in joules. The alley has 11 lanes each returning one such ball, so multiply by 11 for the whole alley. From this total 21 J is subtracted for the energy dissipated in the return ramps, and 26 J is added for the energy stored in the lift belts. Convert the result to kilojoules. What is the final energy figure in kJ?
